title: ESXi host hardening baseline: lockdown mode, no SSH, execInstalledOnly, remote audit logs
summary: Ransomware crews go after hypervisors because one host holds many servers. These are the highest-impact controls from Broadcom's vSphere 8 security configuration guide, with PowerCLI to check and set each one.
steps: Patch first: Broadcom's baseline includes keeping ESXi current and updating vCenter first when an update is available. See VMSA-2026-0006 in the vulnerability watch.

Normal lockdown mode, so all management goes through vCenter: `(Get-View (Get-VMHost -Name $ESXi | Get-View).ConfigManager.HostAccessManager).ChangeLockdownMode('lockdownNormal')`. Review the Exception Users list (`QueryLockdownExceptions()`) first.

Keep SSH and the ESXi Shell stopped and set to manual: `Get-VMHostService -VMHost $ESXi | where {$_.Key -eq 'TSM-SSH'} | Set-VMHostService -Policy Off` (and the same for 'TSM'). Set `UserVars.ESXiShellTimeOut` to 600 and `UserVars.ESXiShellInteractiveTimeOut` to 900.
Only run binaries that come from installed VIBs: `Get-AdvancedSetting VMkernel.Boot.execInstalledOnly | Set-AdvancedSetting -Value True`.

Send logs and audit records off the host: set `Syslog.global.logHost`, `Syslog.global.auditRecord.storageEnable` = True and `Syslog.global.auditRecord.remoteEnable` = True, and use persistent storage rather than /tmp/scratch.
Restrict the ESXi firewall so management services only accept authorized admin networks, and enable management traffic only on management VMkernel adapters (not on vMotion or vSAN).

Turn off services you don't use (SNMP, CIM 'sfcbd-watchdog', SLP 'slpd'). Set Forged Transmits and MAC Address Changes to Reject on standard switches, and require Secure Boot with TPM configuration encryption where the hardware supports it.
pitfalls: Strict lockdown mode means that if the host loses contact with vCenter and you can't restore it, you must rebuild the host. Broadcom says Normal usually suffices.
Backup and monitoring tools may need lockdown exception users or temporary unlocks.
execInstalledOnly can stop unsigned third-party software from running.
Secure Boot plus TPM configuration encryption makes traditional root password recovery impossible, so keep a protected admin account.
Some clustered or network workloads legitimately need Forged Transmits or MAC changes, so give them their own port group.
